title: WDL Module Manifest
description: Metadata, content exclusions, and dependencies for a WDL module, stored in `module.json` at the module root.

name.description: The module's display name. Dependency resolution uses the consumer's dependency key rather than this name.

license.description: The module's SPDX license expression, such as `MIT` or `MIT OR Apache-2.0`.

authors.description: Descriptions of the module's authors, conventionally written as `Name <email>`.

description.description: A brief description of what the module does.

repository.description: The canonical Git URL of the module's source repository.

homepage.description: The URL of the module's documentation or landing page, if distinct from `repository`.

entrypoint.description: The WDL file used for a root symbolic import, relative to and contained within the module root. Defaults to `index.wdl`.

readme.description: A Markdown file relative to and contained within the module root. Defaults to `README.md`; `false` indicates that the module has no readme.

exclude.description: Module-relative glob patterns omitting files from module content, validation, hashing, signing, and packaging. Included files cannot import excluded files. The root `module.json` is always included. Defaults to an empty list.

tools.description: The upstream software wrapped by the module, recorded for provenance and license tracking. Tool versions do not determine the module's version.

items.description: An upstream tool wrapped by the module.

version.description: The upstream tool version wrapped by this module.

license.description: The upstream tool's SPDX license identifier.

url.description: The URL of the upstream tool's homepage, documentation, repository, or canonical project page.

ids.description: External tool identifiers in `prefix:reference` CURIE form, using prefixes registered with identifiers.org or the Bioregistry, such as `biotools:csvkit`.

dependencies.description: Modules keyed by consumer-chosen names. Keys must be valid WDL identifiers after replacing `-` with `_`, and must remain unique after that normalization.

propertyNames.description: A consumer-chosen dependency name used in symbolic imports; it need not match the dependency's `name` field.

additionalProperties.description: A Git dependency with exactly one of `version`, `tag`, `branch`, or `commit`, or a local `path` dependency without a version selector.

oneOf.description: A Git dependency selected by a semantic version requirement.

git.description: The Git repository URL from which to resolve the module.

version.description: A semantic version requirement without a leading `v`, such as `^1.2.0`. Resolution selects the highest matching version tag.

path.description: The module directory relative to and contained within the Git repository root. If omitted, the module is at the repository root.

oneOf.description: A Git dependency selected by an exact tag name.

git.description: The Git repository URL from which to resolve the module.

tag.description: The exact Git tag name, such as `v1.2.0-rc1`. This selector does not use semantic version resolution.

path.description: The module directory relative to and contained within the Git repository root. If omitted, the module is at the repository root.

oneOf.description: A Git dependency selected by a branch name.

git.description: The Git repository URL from which to resolve the module.

branch.description: The Git branch name to resolve. The lockfile records the exact commit selected at resolution time.

path.description: The module directory relative to and contained within the Git repository root. If omitted, the module is at the repository root.

oneOf.description: A Git dependency selected by a commit SHA or a unique prefix of one.

git.description: The Git repository URL from which to resolve the module.

commit.description: A Git commit SHA or a prefix that uniquely identifies a commit in the source repository. The lockfile records the full 40-character SHA.

path.description: The module directory relative to and contained within the Git repository root. If omitted, the module is at the repository root.

oneOf.description: A local module used as-is without a version selector.

path.description: The local module directory, containing its own `module.json`. A relative path is resolved from the consuming module root.
